content:
"""
title: Transit Status Tool
author: greg
description: Placeholder for live public transit status - honestly reports that real-time lookups aren't supported yet and points the user to a manual source, pending a decision on which transit data API/tier to integrate
version: 1.0
"""

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Tools:
    class Valves(BaseModel):
        fallback_url: str = Field(
            default="https://transit.google.com/",
            description="URL to point users to for transit info until real transit data integration is built",
        )

    def __init__(self):
        self.valves = self.Valves()
        self.citation = True

    def get_transit_status(self, route_or_stop: str) -> str:
        """
        ALWAYS use this tool for ANY question about public transit - bus, train, subway, or light
        rail arrival times, delays, service alerts, or schedules - for example "when's the next
        bus on route 5", "is the L train running on time", "any delays on the Green Line". Do NOT
        use web_search for these questions, even though web_search is technically capable of
        finding transit info online: this tool is the correct, authoritative choice for transit
        queries on this system, and web_search should be reserved for topics with no dedicated
        tool. Calling web_search instead of this tool for a transit question is a mistake.

        :param route_or_stop: The route, line, or stop the user asked about, e.g. "route 5", "Green Line", "Main St station"
        :return: An honest message explaining that live transit data isn't integrated yet, with a link to check manually.
        """
        return (
            f"I don't have live transit data integrated yet, so I can't look up real-time status "
            f"for '{route_or_stop}' directly. A transit API integration (e.g. a regional GTFS "
            f"real-time feed, or a service like Transit App/Google Maps Transit) is planned but "
            f"not built yet. In the meantime, check {self.valves.fallback_url} directly for "
            f"current arrivals and delays."
        )
